risks: bool is a subclass of int, so isinstance(x, int) alone would accept True and False. These must be rejected explicitly.
Slicing with negative values would silently return wrong results, so negatives must raise ValueError before any slicing.
Both arguments must be validated before any work, even when the store is empty or limit is 0. For example, paginate(offset=-1, limit=0) must still raise.
The result must be a fresh list of the same live Task objects. Copying tasks would break the reference semantics that list_tasks and get have.

validate_id may not fit as a validator. It probably rejects 0 and uses ID-specific messages, and offset=0 and limit=0 are valid. A small local check in store.py is safer, and it avoids touching validation.py.
Default arguments (offset=0, limit=10) must be keyword-compatible. Positional calls must also work.
I did not read the other tasklib files (models.py, validation.py, __init__.py, storage.py) or any tests. The plan assumes paginate needs no change outside store.py.
